Using EV/EBITDA of 8.84× — the correct primary yardstick for capital-intensive steel per the sector card, where mid-cycle fair value is 5–8× — SAIL sits modestly above the midpoint of that range; the forward P/E of 11.45× (vs trailing 22.32×) signals material earnings growth expected, suggesting the market is not pricing in deterioration, and on EV/EBITDA the valuation is fair-to-slightly-stretched, further constrained by a structural ROE of only 5.7% and ROCE of 8.2% that trails cost of capital. The biggest risk is that net debt of ₹21,018 cr (1.7× EBITDA) leaves limited financial buffer against a margin squeeze from rising crude costs ($92/bbl is a direct coking-coal/energy headwind), while a ₹1,146 cr contingent Jharkhand water-rate liability (High Court LPA 540/2024 pending) and continued FII selling add near-term downside pressure.

Applying the Sector Card yardstick of P/B vs sustainable ROE: IOB trades at 1.83× P/B with TTM ROE of 15.7% — this screens as cheap (P/B < 1.5× with ROE > 12% = cheap per the desk rule; IOB is marginally above that P/B floor but still well below the 3× threshold for expensive), and the peer analysis confirms it sits at P10 on trailing P/E (13.1× vs broad market median 35.4×) and P14 on P/B, placing it unambiguously in the cheap quartile versus peers, although the forward P/E at 39.1× (P80 percentile) is a cautionary signal that the market anticipates earnings normalisation once one-off tax/DTA tailwinds fade. The single biggest fundamental risk is that the reported PAT improvement is substantially driven by non-recurring items — DTA reversals, tax-rate transition, and subsidiary wind-up proceeds — meaning sustainable normalised earnings power may be materially lower than headline figures suggest, and any re-rating toward fair value requires IOB to demonstrate clean, recurring earnings growth while managing the ₹3.6L cr+ contingent tax dispute overhang and continued capital adequacy under accelerating loan growth.

fundamental.thesis: LatentView Analytics is a pure-play data analytics and AI services company serving approximately 30 Fortune 500 clients, with 28% of FY26 revenue now from AI projects — a concentrated, high-engagement book where depth is a differentiator but also a single-point-of-failure risk. FY26 full-year revenue reached ₹1,060 cr (+24.3% YoY), decelerating from +32.3% in FY25 and +31.9% in Q1FY26 — a clear deceleration trend; more critically, PAT grew only +7.4% as EBITDA margins compressed sharply from 31.2% (FY25) to 22.3% (FY26), driven by aggressive AI-and-Databricks investment spending, widening a troubling gap between revenue and profit trajectory. At trailing P/E of 32.3× (above the 22–30× IT sector benchmark), valuation is modestly stretched on a snapshot basis, though forward P/E of 22.1× and broad-peer rank at P46 both point to 'fairly valued' if the embedded earnings-recovery thesis plays out; the stock sitting at 22.7% of its 52-week range does reduce the multiple-compression sting at current entry. The pre-derating setup is real: sell-side EPS estimates have been cut consistently (-2.5% in 30 days, -4.9% next-FY over 90 days) while management offers no numerical guidance, only qualitative AI investment commentary — a pattern that historically precedes a re-rating lower.

fundamental.thesis: Adani Energy Solutions is India's largest private-sector power-transmission company, also operating Mumbai's electricity distribution (AEML) and a fast-growing smart-metering business — sitting at the intersection of India's grid build-out and smart-infrastructure themes with ₹71,779 cr of transmission projects under construction and a ₹29,519 cr smart-meter order book. FY26 operational revenue growth decelerated sharply to +7.3% YoY (from +26.8% in Q1FY26), though adjusted PAT surged 32% to ₹2,393 cr — partly base-effect flattery from an FY25 Dahanu carve-out exceptional item (₹1,506 cr); the distribution segment is a drag, with EBITDA down 3.1% YoY, and total-income growth (15.9%) substantially exceeds operational-revenue growth (7.3%), flagging reliance on SCA construction-revenue recognition. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive utility (as the sector card directs), 25.1× sits at the P55 peer percentile — not egregious in isolation — but the trailing P/E of 81.7× is 5–8× the Utilities sector median of 10–18×, P/B of 7.2× against ROE of only 9.7% signals a value-trap dynamic, and the stock is already at 89.5% of its 52-week range, suggesting the execution optionality is extensively priced in. The single biggest risk is the extreme balance-sheet leverage (D/E 194.5×), which leaves earnings acutely sensitive to any interest-rate shock, project-execution slip, or Adani group governance event that triggers a credit re-pricing.
